newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-VALENZUELA WINS EIGHTH STRAIGHT AS PADRES BEAT CARDS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-VALENZUELA WINS EIGHTH STRAIGHT AS PADRES BEAT CARDS.

text.p: Fernando Valenzuela won his eighth straight decision and Wally Joyner hit a three-run homer in the sixth inning as the San Diego Padres halted the St Louis Cardinals' eight-game winning streak with a 5-4 win on Sunday.
Valenzuela (13-7) allowed two runs and five hits for the Padres, who moved into a first-place tie in the National League West with the Dodgers.
John Mabry's two-run single in the fourth built a 2-0 lead for the Cards, who remained 1 1/2 games ahead of Houston atop the N.L. Central.

In the sixth, Steve Finley and Ken Caminiti walked with one out and Greg Vaughn had an RBI single to bring San Diego within 2-1. Joyner followed with his eighth homer of the season to give the Padres a 4-2 lead.
Pinch-hitter Rickey Henderson then walked and scored San Diego's fifth run on Tony Gwynn's double.

Trevor Hoffman started the ninth and gave up a single to Brian Jordan on his first pitch and Gary Gaetti's 20th homer on his next offering. But Hoffman got the next three batters in order for his 35th save.
Todd Stottlemyre (12-11) gave up four runs and five hits with three walks and seven strikeouts in seven innings and took the loss for the Cardinals.
In Los Angeles, pinch-hitter Orlando Merced snapped a ninth-inning tie with a bases-loaded double as the Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Dodgers, snapping their six-game win streak.
Scott Radinsky replaced Darren Dreifort (1-3) and Merced hit the first pitch into deep right-centre field to clear the bases.
Mike Piazza tied the game at 1-1 in the seventh with his 33rd homer.
Dan Plesac (4-5) picked up the win with one inning of scoreless relief. John Ericks allowed two hits in the ninth, but retired the final three batters to record his fifth save.
At Florida, Gary Sheffield hit a two-run homer, his 41st, and newly acquired Rick Helling and two relievers combined on a four-hitter as the Marlins edged the Montreal Expos 2-1.
The loss dropped the Expos into a tie in the N.L. wild card race with the Padres and Dodgers.
Helling went seven innings, allowing one run and four hits while tying a career-high with nine strikeouts.
Jay Powell pitched a scoreless eighth before Robb Nen retired the side in order in the ninth for his 31st save.
Montreal's Pedro Martinez (12-10) struck out nine in seven innings. He allowed two runs and six hits.

In Atlanta, Todd Hundley became the first Met to hit 40 homers in a season, tying Roy Campanella's major-league record for home runs by a catcher, and Mark Clark outpitched Greg Maddux as the New York Mets beat the Braves 6-2.
"It feels like a thousand pounds have been lifted from my shoulders," Hundley said.
Clark went eight innings allowing two runs and four hits, including Chipper Jones's two-run homer, with five strikeouts and three walks. John Franco pitched a scoreless ninth.
Maddux, who like Clark moved to 13-11, gave up five runs, seven hits and one walk in five innings.
In Houston, Andres Galarraga drove in a pair of runs, including one in a tie-breaking three-run ninth inning that led the Colorado Rockies to a 5-2 win over the Astros.
Houston dropped four games behind the Expos in the wild-card chase.

Steve Reed (4-3), the last of three Rockies pitchers used in the eighth, retired the only batter he faced to get the win. Bruce Ruffin logged the ninth for his 19th save as Shane Reynolds (16-9) homered, but took the loss.
Reynolds gave up four runs and six hits in eight innings.
In Cincinnati, Barry Larkin and Ed Taubensee both homered in a five-run eighth inning that lifted the Cincinnati Reds to their third straight win 8-3 against the Giants.
After Lee Smith blew a 3-1 lead by allowing two runs in the top of the inning, the Reds struck against three relievers, as Hal Morris also delivered a two-run double.
Jeff Shaw (7-5) got the win, despite allowing Steve Scarsone's two-run infield single in the top of the eighth.
Smith ruined an outstanding performance by starter Dave Burba, who allowed one run and two hits over seven innings.
Barry Bonds hit his 37th homer for San Francisco.
In Philadelphia, Jaime Navarro (15-9) allowed one earned run over six innings for his eighth consecutive victory and Scott Servais drove in three runs as the Chicago Cubs beat the Phillies 5-3.
Navarro (15-9) allowed two runs and seven hits with two walks and four strikeouts. Turk Wendell pitched the ninth for his 17th save and 10th in a row.
Servais opened the scoring in the second inning with a sacrifice fly off Mike Mimbs (2-8), added an RBI fielder's choice in the fourth and drove in Jose Hernandez with an eighth-inning double.
